title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Your voice is a place; speak simply from lived truth so people stay
summary: Andreea Popa argues that sounding smart matters less than being felt, and that a voice is a place people enter and either stay in or leave. She cites Cris Pop's rule from his newsletter, "only teach what you've lived", and builds on it with a case for lived truth and for clarity as respect. Her stories about chasing clever words are her own.

principles.text: Cris's rule: teach only what you have lived, and say it only if it changed you first.
Being understood and changing someone matters more than looking clever; admired but unclear words are not followed or remembered.
principles.quote: People may admire what they don’t understand, but they won’t follow it. They won’t remember it. And they definitely won’t change because of it.

principles.text: Your voice is a place people walk into; if it is not grounded and true, they leave.
principles.quote: Your voice is a place, one people can walk into. Every time you speak or write, you're inviting someone in.

principles.text: Contradicting your own truth costs your message its weight, so stay consistent with what you actually believe.
principles.quote: Break your own truth, and your message loses its weight.

principles.text: Simplifying is respect for the listener, not a dumbing down of complexity.
principles.quote: We don’t simplify because people can’t handle complexity. We simplify because clarity is an act of respect.

principles.text: Speak for the version of yourself who felt small or confused; that is where resonance begins.
principles.quote: Start a piece with a sentence your past self needed to hear.
